summary: Client-side flow window starvation causes late streaming chunks to be suppressed after proxy idle reset
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running streaming responses intermittently truncate the final sentences when a corporate proxy performs an idle connection reset. The problem appears correlated with sustained low client read-window availability (client-side flow control) after the proxy re-establishes the socket, causing the last chunks to be dropped rather than delivered or resumed.

Impact:
- Several production customers using the Dedicated tier (including Acme Analytics) observe missing concluding sentences in SSE streams and websocket streaming responses roughly 0.3-0.8% of long-running requests (>= 60s).
- Affects downstream text generation quality and breaks deterministic post-processing (post-hoc truncation/QA).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod us-east, Node.js SDK v1.8.2 and direct SSE/WS clients behind corporate proxy (HTTP/2+nginx-based edge).
- Observed with models redwood/open-7b-v1 and redwood/opt-6.7b on gpu-medium instances.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Establish SSE stream via fetch with keepalive and low client read buffer (example below).
2) Let model generate for > 60s, then simulate proxy idle reset (nginx keepalive timeout + upstream reconnect).
3) Observe client receives a partial final sentence and no end-event.

Node fetch example used by customer:
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'GET', headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' }, keepalive: true });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) { const { value, done } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; processChunk(value); }

Observed behavior:
- After proxy resets connection, the client-side read window reported by the OS is small for a short duration. The server continues to push remaining tokens but the network path backpressure causes RST/half-close behavior from the proxy that results in the client never seeing the final 1-3 chunks.
- In logs, the serving runtime shows request completed successfully (200/stream_end) and the end-marker emitted, but the client never receives the terminal event.

Expected behavior:
- End-marker or final chunks should be reliably delivered or resumed after reconnect; client should receive terminal event even if a proxy reset occurs mid-stream.

Raw logs (redacted) from customer capture:
[2026-03-11T16:22:17Z] SSE session id=acme-12345 chunk_seq=498 token_count=1245
[2026-03-11T16:23:43Z] edge-proxy idle_timeout reset upstream_reconnect id=acme-12345
[2026-03-11T16:23:44Z] serving-runtime stream_end id=acme-12345 end_marker=0xEOT
[2026-03-11T16:23:44Z] ws-session closed remote=proxy code=1006

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Increase client TCP receive buffer size and enable more aggressive read loop. Reduced but did not eliminate occurrences.
- Switching to shorter generation windows (<=20s) avoided the issue but is not an acceptable product change for them.

Notes for support triage:
- Customer provided a pcap and proxy config. Customer requests a fix or mitigation that does not require changes to their corporate proxy configuration.

investigation_notes: Customer pcap shows FIN from proxy to client during reconnect while origin still streaming.
Reproduction harness: nginx proxy with keepalive_timeout=30s, node fetch with small read loop + artificial CPU pressure replicates missing final chunks.
Serving runtime logs show stream_end and end-marker emitted and acknowledged by upstream (edge), so origin transmission likely not root cause.

Edge-proxy behavior: on upstream reconnect it currently creates new downstream socket before fully draining upstream in-flight buffer in certain HTTP/2 path. This can drop final segments when client read-window is low.

Proposed code mitigations: add server-side end-marker retransmit on consumer reconnect; add small periodic keepalive-end syntactic chunk so partial resumes can reassemble; add instrumentation for downstream FINs correlated with stream_truncate metric.
Observed that customers using tcp_keepalive tweaks or increasing read buffer saw fewer occurrences, indicating client-side window influences severity.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1245 (runtime: end-marker retransmit on reconnect)
resolution:
Mitigation in progress: runtime team implemented an end-marker retransmit guard and a 2s periodic 'tail-heartbeat' chunk. Patch landed in PR 1245 and will be rolled out to the us-east dedicated pool as a staged canary starting 2026-03-16. Customer agreed to canary.

Longer-term: edge-proxy fix planned to gracefully drain upstream buffers before creating new downstream socket on reconnect. Engineering to follow up with timeline and include automatic alert when downstream FINs correlate with stream_truncate metrics.

If customer continues to see occurrences after canary, escalate to emergency rollback/resolution and consider forced TCP-level buffer adjustments in SDK as additional mitigation.
